newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-ARGENTINE JUDGE ORDERS MARADONA'S MANAGER FREED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINE JUDGE ORDERS MARADONA'S MANAGER FREED.

text.p: An Argentine judge on Tuesday ordered the immediate release from prison of soccer star Diego Maradona's manager Guillermo Coppola, who was jailed on drugs charges last year, local media reported.

Judge Carlos Liporaci said there was insufficient evidence to keep Coppola behind bars, where he has been since last October when police said they found a pound (400 g) of cocaine hidden in a vase in a raid on his Buenos Aires apartment.

Coppola, who said the drugs were planted in his apartment, was due to be released from Caseros jail in Buenos Aires later on Tuesday, the DyN news agency said. He was initially accused of drug trafficking but the charge was later modified to possessing drugs and supplying cocaine at a party in his home.

Coppola has maintained his innocence and his lawyer cast doubt on the reliability of the two government witnesses, Samantha Farjat and Natalia de Negri, whose appearances on talk shows have made them among Argentina's best known women.

The Coppola case sparked sordid and often contradictory allegations in the media of celebrity drug-taking and sex, and one witness accused police of blackmailing her to plant drugs in the house of another investigation target -- former soccer player Alberto Tarantini. He was also freed and a top judge's aide and three undercover policemen were arrested.
